name: Laundry sanitiser and strip washing
lead: Laundry sanitiser and strip washing are practices discussed for removing persistent odour from gym and sports clothing. Sanitisers are additives intended to kill microorganisms in the wash, while strip washing is a heavy soak and wash intended to remove built-up residue.

No source reviewed here covers either practice in detail. Wikipedia's laundry article says high temperatures kill microorganisms, though it flags the claim as uncited, and says drying at 60 degrees Celsius or higher for thirty minutes kills many mites.[1] Body odour is generally attributed to bacteria acting on skin secretions, which can transfer to fabric.[2]

paras: Odour-causing bacteria such as Corynebacterium and Staphylococcus species act on sweat secretions.[2] Practitioners seeking to remove the resulting smell from clothes use hotter washes, additives or extended soaks, but the sources reviewed here do not evaluate these methods.

lore.intro: Community accounts describe odour that survives ordinary washing in gym clothes.

claims.claim: Sanitiser or strip washing removes odour that normal washing leaves.
claims.believers: Proponents say clothes smell fresh again after such treatment.
claims.experts: No dedicated studies were found; general references describe heat as reducing microorganisms but without evidence for these methods.[1]

card.summary: Extra washing tricks for smelly gym kit; popular anecdotes, no dedicated studies.
card.note: Check garment care labels; heat can damage some fabrics.

quick.overview:
Some people use sanitising additives or long soaks to get smell out of workout clothes.

No study found here tests these methods.
quick.mechanism: The aim is to kill or wash away odour-producing bacteria and residue; heat and drying are the factors general references mention.
quick.risks: Heat and agitation can shrink or damage some fabrics, so care labels apply.[1]
